name: Mounagiri Hanuman Temple
significance: A modern hilltop Hanuman shrine near Hampapuram in Anantapur district, developed by the Mounagiri Global Trust under Eswaraiah Swamy and consecrated in November 2010. Around a thousand artisans and five hundred volunteers worked on it, the main Hanuman image alone costing some 90 lakh rupees.

name: Baba Ranadhir Temple
deity: Baba Ranadhir, a saint venerated as a healer
significance: A shrine at Bhuna in Haryana's Fatehabad district raised in homage to Baba Ranadhir, an early saint remembered for healing the afflicted. Thursday is its principal day of visitation.
story: Devotees hold that a sprinkle of water from the shrine's tank cures every kind of skin affliction.

name: Alarnatha Temple
deity: Vishnu as Alarnath Dev, with a shrine to Mahalakshmi
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Brahmagiri, some 23 km from Puri, counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetras. It is associated with Ramanujacharya's journey through Odisha and preserves a stone slab linked to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's sankirtana.
story: Devotees say Jagannath directed Chaitanya Mahaprabhu here during Anavasara, the fortnight when the Puri image is withdrawn from view and the lord is believed to appear instead as Alarnath.

name: ISKCON Temple, Patna
significance: An ISKCON temple on Buddha Marg in Patna whose foundation stone was laid in 2007 and which opened in phases, the first in May 2022 and the remainder in 2023, at a cost of roughly 100 crore rupees. Subsidiary shrines hold Gaura-Nitai and Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman.

name: Boyakonda Gangamma Temple
significance: A hill shrine above Diguvapalli in Chowdepalli mandal, Annamayya district, built and long maintained by the Boya and Pala Ekari communities of the surrounding forest. It passed to the Andhra Pradesh Endowments Department in 1990.
story: The goddess is said to have come down from the hillock to shield the forest communities from a Nawab's soldiers, destroying his army and hanging the heads of the slain on the branches of a banyan.

name: Dhirdham Temple
style: Nepali, modelled on the Pashupatinath Temple at Kathmandu
significance: A Shiva temple at Darjeeling built in 1939 by Rai Saheb Purna Bahadur Pradhan of Nepal. Beg Raj Shakya designed it as a smaller echo of the Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu.

name: Kolaramma Temple
deity: Kolaramma, with a second shrine to Chelamma the scorpion goddess
significance: A goddess temple at Kolar raised about a thousand years ago by the Talakad Gangas and enlarged under the Cholas, whose inscriptions and granite reliefs, including one of Rajendra Chola I in battle, survive on its walls. The Mysore maharajas were later patrons.
story: Worshippers hold that praying at the Chelamma shrine keeps a person safe from scorpion stings.

name: Kamaldah Jain Temple
significance: A Shvetambara Jain temple built at Patna in 1729 to commemorate the acharya Sthulabhadra, with a second shrine dedicated to Sudarshana and an inscription of 1792. It is a fixture of Bihar's Jain pilgrimage circuit.
story: The temple is believed to stand on the ground where Sthulabhadra, successor of Bhadrabahu, spent his last days.

name: Gurdwara Nada Sahib
deity: Guru Granth Sahib; commemorates Guru Gobind Singh's halt here
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; marks a halt of 1688
significance: A gurdwara in Panchkula district marking the spot where Guru Gobind Singh halted while travelling from Paonta Sahib to Anandpur Sahib after the Battle of Bhangani in 1688, his first battle, fought at nineteen. The site lay forgotten until a villager, Bhai Motha Singh, raised a platform on it; management passed to the PEPSU Dharmarth Board in 1948 and to the SGPC after 1956.

name: Shantinath Shiva Temple
significance: An 1828 nine-pinnacled nava-ratna Shiva temple in the Mitrasenpur quarter of Chandrakona, roughly nineteen and a half feet square and protected as a state monument. Its terracotta panels carry Ramayana battle scenes, Krishna lila, Bhishma on his bed of arrows, the Dashavatara and rows of musicians.

name: Katta Maisamma Temple
deity: Katta Maisamma, a manifestation of Shakti
significance: A goddess shrine raised beside a tank bund by the Golconda Patel family when the bund was built, its name taken from katta, the bund itself. The Nizams offered here in the month of Ashadha for the safety of the kingdom, and the sixth Nizam, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, made an offering on the banks of the Musi during the flood of 1908.
story: The 1908 flood is said to have subsided the moment the Nizam completed his offering to the goddess.

name: Kodlamane Vishnumurthy Temple
place: Kodlamane, Honnavar taluk, Uttara Kannada district
significance: A Vishnu temple at Kodlamane in Honnavar taluk of Uttara Kannada district, about a kilometre from Idagunji and 23 km from Honnavar town. A natural stream called Vishnu Tirtha runs beside it.
story: The shrine is said to have been found several centuries ago deep inside dense hill forest.

name: Lakshmeshwara Jain Temples
deity: Neminatha at the Shankha Basadi and Anantanatha at the Anantanatha Basadi
dynasty: Badami Chalukya; Western Ganga; Kalyani Chalukya
style: Badami Chalukya, with rekhanagara and phamsana shikharas
significance: A group of Jain basadis at Lakshmeshwara in Gadag district, known in antiquity as Puligere or Hugligere, of which the Shankha Basadi dates from the 7th century and the Anantanatha Basadi from about the 12th. Inscriptions of the 7th and 8th centuries record grants to them, and Kunkuma Mahadevi, sister of Vijayaditya, built a large Jain temple here in the reign of Kirtivarman II.

name: Gurdwara Dukh Nivaran Sahib
deity: Guru Granth Sahib; commemorates the visit of Guru Tegh Bahadur
significance: A Patiala gurdwara on the ground of the old village of Lehal, where Guru Tegh Bahadur stayed beneath a banyan tree on 24 January 1672. Raja Amar Singh laid out a memorial garden on the spot, Maharaja Bhupinder Singh had a proposed railway line moved so the tree would survive, and Maharaja Yadavindra Singh built the present shrine and sarovar between 1930 and 1942.
story: The villagers of Lehal are said to have begged the Guru to come because a mysterious sickness was killing them, and devotees still hold the water of the sarovar to be healing.

name: Umamaheshwaram Temple
significance: A Shiva temple set in the Nallamala forest about 4 km from Rangapur village near Achampet, some 100 km from Hyderabad. It is regarded as the northern gateway to Srisailam, one of the twelve jyotirlingas.
